; -*- mode: Org;-*-

#+TITLE: 03 emacs bundle — build devbase + emacs tarballs on c02, ship as archive bundles
#+STARTUP: overview

* Dev process setup
  Before executing ANY work item in this plan, open and obey
  the rules defined in this project's per-repo instructions:

    - .github/copilot-instructions.md  (mirrored in CLAUDE.md)

  Both auto-load into every GHCP CLI session.  Read the current
  rules there and follow them.  This plan intentionally does
  not restate any rule — the per-repo instructions are the
  single source of truth.

  :THE_THREE_THAT_BITE_HERE, by name only — read them there, not here:
  R-MEASURE (a number you did not run is not a number), R-FLEET (a
  per-box row, never a fleet verdict), R-REPEATABLE (anything that
  CHANGES state on a box is a script in bin/, fanned out — not a
  one-liner typed twice).

* Goal
  Emacs 30.1 (+tree-sitter) and the devbase toolchain are installed and
  runnable in BOTH tiers on the fleet:

    - the WSL side (ubuntu 24.04), and
    - the container side (azurelinux 3.0 / arcadia),

  delivered the way this repo already delivers binaries that a target
  cannot install for itself: as ROOT-EXTRACTABLE TARBALLS committed to
  =archive/=, unpacked by a =bin/= script.

  Done means, measured per box (never a fleet verdict):
    - =emacs --version= answers in the WSL tier AND inside the container
    - the devbase language servers answer (=typescript-language-server
      --version=, =jedi-language-server --version=)
    - ssh into the box still works after the drop-in (config + keys
      intact), and =.bashrc= sources cleanly with no dead endpoint
    - the four tarballs are committed under =archive/= and pushed

* Dependencies
  Ground truth MEASURED 2026-09-13, not assumed.  Re-measure before
  trusting any of it; every line below is a command that was run.

  - :BUILD_BOX: c02 — USER RULING, supersedes the c01 draft.
    :USER_VERBATIM_2026-09-13: "if ghcp already ready on c02, we only
    need plan . push, and I can ssh to c02wsl exec the plan inside CLI"
    So this plan's deliverable is ITSELF: author + commit + push, and the
    user runs it from a GHCP CLI session on c02wsl.  Do NOT execute the
    build from here.
    MEASURED on c02: GHCP CLI 1.0.84-2 present; /workspace/dot-emacs
    ALREADY CLONED with all 11 build/ dirs; /workspace/bundles exists
    (holds lserver.tgz).  /workspace/cluster is NOT there yet.
    :trap: the existing c02 clone reports =fatal: detected dubious
    ownership in repository= — it is owned by another user, so git
    refuses it.  Fix with =git config --global --add safe.directory
    /workspace/dot-emacs= (or re-clone) BEFORE trusting any rev-parse.
    c01 measurement kept for reference — it MEASURED both base images
    present plus 922G free, so it remains a valid fallback build box:
      #+begin_src bash
      .github/skills/fleet_ssh/fleet-ssh.sh -b c01 \
        CEJ='docker images --format "{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}" | grep -c codeexecutionjupyterext1' \
        UBU='docker images --format "{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}" | grep -c "^ubuntu:24.04"' \
        DISK='df -h / | tail -1 | tr -s " " | cut -d" " -f4'
      # c01  1  1  922G
      #+end_src

  - :SOURCE_REPO: bartuer/dot-emacs.  The build recipes live in its
    =build/= folder and are AUTHORITATIVE; this plan does not reinvent
    them.  HTTPS reachability MEASURED from c01 (=git ls-remote=
    returned a674fa50 on refs/heads).

  - :CLONE_OVER_SSH_NOT_HTTPS — USER RULING, and it is load-bearing.
    :USER_VERBATIM_2026-09-13: "the clone should use ssh key, then we
    can push fix back to github, I mean clone in c02"
    WHY it matters here and is not a preference: this plan MODIFIES
    dot-emacs (2.5 rewrites bashrc_patch's endpoint, 2.6 fixes the
    ssh-asset modes).  Those fixes belong upstream, and an HTTPS clone
    cannot push them back.  So:
        git clone git@github.com:bartuer/dot-emacs /workspace/dot-emacs
    :trap: THIS DOES NOT WORK ON ANY BOX TODAY — MEASURED:
        ssh -T git@github.com  ->  Permission denied (publickey)
        ls ~/.ssh/id_*         ->  0 keys, root AND human tier
        test -f ~/.ssh/nx.rsa  ->  NO on c01, c02, c03, c04
        grep ^Host github.com ~/.ssh/config -> 0 on all four
    So a github ssh key is a PRECONDITION of this plan, not a detail
    inside it — see 1.0, which now gates Group 1.
    THE KEY AND THE CONFIG ARE BOTH KNOWN — user ruling:
    :USER_VERBATIM_2026-09-13: "and dot-emacs need a special configure
    like add a host github in ssh configure then git push will work,
    nx.rsa works for github"
    VERIFIED from this container: =ssh -i ~/.ssh/nx.rsa -T git@github.com=
    -> "Hi bartuer! You've successfully authenticated" — i.e. nx.rsa is
    already a github key for the ACCOUNT THAT OWNS dot-emacs, so no new
    key needs minting.  What is missing on the boxes is (a) the key file
    and (b) a Host block telling ssh to use it:
        Host github.com
             User git
             IdentityFile ~/.ssh/nx.rsa
             IdentitiesOnly yes
             StrictHostKeyChecking no
    :trap: =IdentitiesOnly yes= matters.  Without it ssh offers every
    key in the agent first and github can reject the connection on
    too-many-auth-failures BEFORE it ever reaches nx.rsa — which reads
    as "the key is wrong" when the key is fine.
    :trap: the pre-existing /workspace/dot-emacs on c02 has NO origin
    remote readable (dubious-ownership refusal) — do not assume it is an
    ssh clone just because it exists.  Re-point or re-clone it.

  - :FOUR_TARGETS: exactly four of the build/ subfolders matter here:
    | folder                                                  | produces                                 |
    |---------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
    | devbox-ubuntu-24.04                                     | devbase, WSL tier                        |
    | emacs-30.1-treesitter-ubuntu-24.04                      | amd64.emacs30.1_24.04.tar.gz             |
    | devbox-arcadia-azurelinux-3.0-photon-5.0                | devbase, container tier                  |
    | emacs-30.1-treesitter-arcadia-azurelinux-3.0-photon-5.0 | amd64.arcadia.emacs30.1_azl3.0.tar.gz    |

  - :BUILD_CONTRACT: each folder is =docker build= then =./pack.sh=;
    =pack.sh= bind-mounts =$PWD= to /opt and runs =tar.sh= inside the
    image, so the tarball lands beside the Dockerfile.  Tarballs are
    extractable at filesystem root (=tar ... -C /=).

  - :NO_PRIVATE_FEED_AUTH_NEEDED.  MEASURED, and it CANCELS a work item
    this plan would otherwise have carried.  grep over the whole build/
    tree for =pkgs.visualstudio / @1js / _packaging / npmrc / pip.conf /
    index-url= returns NOTHING in any of the four target Dockerfiles.
    The npm/pip installs are public packages (typescript,
    typescript-language-server, prettier, eslint, jedi-language-server,
    jupyter...).  The only private-feed string in the repo is a NUGET
    line in build/project.org.txt, which is prose and not on any build
    path here.
    So =bin/npm-auth.sh= (the AugmentationLoop feed minter proven for the
    officeagent/api-server build on c02) is NOT a dependency of this
    plan.  Keep it in mind as the fallback if a build ever does start
    resolving a scoped package — it already proves the credential route
    (git credential fill for dev.azure.com -> base64 into _password),
    so that would be a known, solved problem rather than a blocker.

  - :BASE_IMAGE_IS_PUBLIC.  =mcr.microsoft.com/officepy/codeexecutionjupyterext1=
    is docker-pull-ready with no login (user ruling, then MEASURED:
    =docker pull -q= succeeded on c01, which had zero copies before).
    This REMOVED the cross-box constraint this plan first assumed —
    c01 had ubuntu:24.04 and c02 had the officepy images, and an earlier
    draft was about to split the build across two boxes for no reason.

  - :PRECEDENT: (link "/workspace/research/cluster/bin/container-tmux.sh" 0)
    is the shape to copy.  It is the third bundle in =archive/= and it
    documents WHY bundles exist here at all: the RUNNING arcadia
    container cannot reach its own package repo ("Failed to synchronize
    cache for repo 'Azure Linux Official Cloud Native 3.0'"), so
    =tdnf install= is not an option inside it.
    :trap: that is true of the RUNNING container and NOT of the BUILD
    image — measured, =docker run --rm <azl3 image> tdnf list gcc=
    resolves gcc 13.2.0-7.azl3, and ubuntu:24.04 apt-get update works.
    Build-time network is fine; run-time network is not.  That asymmetry
    is exactly why we build a tarball instead of installing in place.

* Context
  - :ARCHIVE_CONVENTION: =archive/= already holds lserver.tar.gz (26 MB),
    wwwrootsdx.tar.gz (6.5 MB), container-tmux.tar.gz (470 KB).  New
    bundles join them there; a =bin/= script unpacks each.

  - :SIZE_IS_THE_RISK.  container-tmux is 470 KB because tmux is ONE
    binary with two libs already in the base.  Emacs + a devbase
    toolchain is a different order of magnitude and these are committed
    to git.  MEASURE each tarball before committing and record the
    number; if a bundle is large enough to hurt the clone, say so in the
    findings rather than committing silently.
    :trap: the relay is ~50 KB/s container->C01 and ~68 KB/s helix->box
    (measured earlier this session).  Anything big moves box-to-box over
    the c01<->c02 mesh (~95 MB/s), or it does not move at all.

  - :SSH_AND_BASHRC_ARE_ALREADY_IN_THE_TARBALL.  devbox-ubuntu-24.04's
    pack.sh explicitly appends =/root/.ssh/config=,
    =/root/.ssh/authorized_keys=, =find /etc/ssh=, and =/root/.bashrc=
    to its file list.  So "make sure ssh config and bashrc work" is
    mostly a VERIFY step, not an author step — but see the next item,
    which is a live bug.

  - :BASHRC_PATCH_SHIPS_A_DEAD_IP — FOUND WHILE MEASURING, must be fixed
    before anything is shipped.  build/bashrc_patch contains:
        export COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL="http://172.25.159.143:11434/v1"
    =172.25.159.143= is the STALE WSL IP that caused this session's
    helix port-22 outage (two netsh portproxy rules forwarding to a dead
    WSL address; see
    (link "/workspace/research/cluster/.github/REPL/fix.archive/helix-port22-cutover-postmortem.md" 0)).
    Shipping it bakes a dead endpoint into every box's .bashrc.
    It also pins COPILOT_MODEL="claude-opus-4-7".
    :trap: a dead PROVIDER_BASE_URL does not fail loudly at shell
    start — .bashrc sources fine and the breakage only appears later,
    when the CLI tries to reach the provider.  So "bashrc sources
    cleanly" is NOT sufficient evidence; the endpoint must be probed.

* TODO Group 1 — clone and stage on c02
** TODO 1.0 GATE: a github ssh key that can PUSH must exist on c02
   Everything in Group 2 that fixes dot-emacs depends on this.  Do it
   first; do not start building and discover at push time.
   TWO PARTS, both measured missing on every box: the KEY FILE and the
   HOST BLOCK (see :CLONE_OVER_SSH_NOT_HTTPS: for the exact block and
   why IdentitiesOnly is required).
   #+begin_src bash
   # 1. ship the key (stdin, never argv -- see trap below)
   ssh c02wsl 'umask 077; mkdir -p ~/.ssh; cat > ~/.ssh/nx.rsa' < ~/.ssh/nx.rsa
   ssh c02wsl 'chmod 600 ~/.ssh/nx.rsa'
   # 2. add the Host block, then PROVE it
   ssh c02wsl 'ssh -o BatchMode=yes -T git@github.com 2>&1 | head -1'
   # want: "Hi bartuer! You've successfully authenticated..."
   # today: "Permission denied (publickey)."   <- MEASURED 2026-09-13
   #+end_src
   :trap: key material travels over ssh/scp ONLY, never through a
   command whose argv is logged — the same rule bin/npm-auth.sh follows
   for the feed token.  The =cat >= form above keeps it off the argv.
   :trap: R-REPEATABLE — this CHANGES state on a box, so once it works
   for c02 it belongs in a bin/ script fanned out, not typed per box.
   :trap: an ssh key that authenticates is not automatically a key that
   can PUSH to this repo; verify write access, not just auth.

               && cd /workspace/dot-emacs && git rev-parse --short HEAD'

** TODO 1.3 :test_tool: build-probe — one command, four answers
   Write =bin/emacs-bundle-status.sh= that prints ONE line per tier with
   the four facts that matter, so the main loop has a single
   fast read.  Model it on container-tmux.sh's output shape
   (=host KEY=value=), and probe the ARTIFACT not the package db:
     - emacs --version in WSL
     - emacs --version in the container
     - typescript-language-server --version
     - jedi-language-server --version
   :trap: probe with the binary, never with =dpkg -s= / =rpm -q= — an
   unpacked-but-unrunnable emacs passes a file-existence test and fails
   the only test that matters.  container-tmux.sh makes this exact point
   and then asserts a real tmux SESSION rather than =tmux -V=.

* TODO Group 2 — fix the inputs, then build the four tarballs on c02
  ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: 2.1 and 2.2 edit files that the builds BAKE IN
  (bashrc_patch's endpoint, the ssh-asset modes).  Building first means
  building twice — the tarball is only correct if the fix landed before
  =docker build= read the context.
  Then ubuntu first.  Its base image was already local and its
  Dockerfile is the simpler of the two, so a failure there is cheaper to
  diagnose than one in the arcadia multi-stage build.

  :DEVIATION_2026-09-14: this session's user explicitly scoped
  execution to THREE of the four builds — emacs-ubuntu (2.3),
  emacs-arcadia (2.5), devbase-arcadia (2.6) — and to THIS box, not
  c02.  =c02wsl= was unreachable from here (no ssh alias resolves it;
  the mesh config only has =C01=/=C02=, and neither carries a github
  key or a =/workspace/dot-emacs= clone reachable over that path from
  this session).  This box (=c01wsl=, container tier) already had a
  clean HTTPS clone of dot-emacs with the four target Dockerfiles
  present, direct (non-proxied) internet, Docker with 909G free, and
  32 CPUs — sufficient to build and smoke-test natively.  So Group 1
  (clone-on-c02, ssh key gating) is SKIPPED for this run; 2.1/2.2/2.3/
  2.5/2.6 were done LOCALLY instead.  2.4 (devbox-ubuntu-24.04) was
  NOT requested and is left TODO.  Group 3 (copy off c02 into
  archive/, commit, push) and Group 4 (drop-in + verify on the fleet)
  still assume the c02/fleet topology and are UNCHANGED/TODO — a
  future session should decide whether to adapt them to "artifacts
  already sit in this repo's build/ dirs" or to still stage through
  c02 as originally planned.

** DONE 2.1 fix the dead IP in bashrc_patch (INPUT FIX — before any build)
   DONE 2026-09-14, executed LOCALLY (not on c02 — see Group-1 deviation
   note at the top of this group).  Fixed all THREE occurrences of the
   literal =172.25.159.143= for =COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=:
   =build/bashrc_patch=,
   =build/emacs-30.1-treesitter-arcadia-azurelinux-3.0-photon-5.0/.bashrc=,
   =build/devbox-arcadia-azurelinux-3.0-photon-5.0/.bashrc= — all now read
   =http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1=.  Left the unrelated
   =Host host / Hostname 172.25.159.143= line in
   =devbox-arcadia-azurelinux-3.0-photon-5.0/config= untouched — that is a
   different SSH alias, not the Copilot provider endpoint this item
   targets.  Endpoint liveness (=curl .../v1/models=) NOT re-probed here;
   that is 4.5's job.
   See :BASHRC_PATCH_SHIPS_A_DEAD_IP: above.
   :interrupt_TAKEN_AND_CLOSED: — the user ruled on the endpoint.
   :USER_VERBATIM_2026-09-13: "yes good catch should use the
   host.docker.internal"
   So the literal =172.25.159.143= becomes =host.docker.internal=:
       export COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL="http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1"
   WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE, not just a different literal: a NAME is
   resolved per-box at run time, so one .bashrc is correct on every box
   and survives a WSL IP change — which is the exact failure that
   produced the dead 172.25.159.143 in the first place.
   MEASURED on c02: =getent hosts host.docker.internal= -> 10.4.0.10
   (resolves, and is NOT the dead address).
   :trap: resolving is not answering.  MEASURED the same run,
   =curl http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1/models= -> DOWN on c02.
   So 4.5's endpoint probe is a REAL check that currently FAILS there;
   bringing the provider up is its own task, not silently part of this
   one.  Also re-check COPILOT_MODEL="claude-opus-4-7" against what that
   endpoint actually serves.

** DONE 2.2 fix the ssh-asset MODES, 755 -> 644 (INPUT FIX — before any build)
   DONE 2026-09-14.  MEASURED: the source files
   =devbox-arcadia-azurelinux-3.0-photon-5.0/{config,authorized_keys}=
   were ALREADY 644 in git/on disk when this session started (fixed in
   an earlier, untracked session — no commit history shows it). Added
   the choke-point fix this plan calls for anyway, for defense in depth:
       COPY --chmod=644 config /root/.ssh/config
       COPY --chmod=644 authorized_keys /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
   in =devbox-arcadia-azurelinux-3.0-photon-5.0/Dockerfile=.  VERIFIED IN
   THE TARBALL per the trap below: =tar tvzf
   amd64.arcadia.dev.base.azl3.0.tar.gz | grep root/.ssh= shows
   =-rw-r--r--= on both =config= and =authorized_keys=.
   USER RULING.  :USER_VERBATIM_2026-09-13: "the authorized_keys and
   config should be chmod to 644, current tar ball has not fix that"
   MEASURED in the build tree, and it is NOT uniform — which is why a
   blanket "chmod everything" would be the wrong fix:
   | folder                                   | authorized_keys / config |
   |------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
   | devbox-ubuntu-24.04                      | 644 — already correct    |
   | emacs-30.1-treesitter-ubuntu-24.04       | 644 — already correct    |
   | devbox-arcadia-azurelinux-3.0-photon-5.0 | 755 — WRONG, fix this    |
   ROOT CAUSE, found by reading the Dockerfile rather than guessing:
   devbox-arcadia .../Dockerfile:112-113 does a bare
       COPY config /root/.ssh/config
       COPY authorized_keys /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
   with no =--chmod= and no following =chmod=, so Docker PRESERVES the
   source file's 755.  Line 101 chmods /root/.ssh to 700 but never the
   files inside it.
   Fix at the choke point — in the Dockerfile, so the tarball is born
   correct rather than repaired after unpacking:
       COPY --chmod=644 config /root/.ssh/config
       COPY --chmod=644 authorized_keys /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
   and normalize the two source files in git as well (=chmod 644=), so a
   future builder that copies plainly still gets 644.
   :trap: 755 on these is not cosmetic.  sshd REFUSES an overly
   permissive config/authorized_keys and falls back to no-key auth — the
   failure surfaces as "Permission denied (publickey)" on a box whose
   key material is present and correct, which is a deeply misleading
   symptom.
   :trap: VERIFY IN THE TARBALL, not in the build context.  =tar tvzf=
   shows the shipped mode; that is the artifact the box will unpack:
   #+begin_src bash
   tar tvzf <devbase>.tar.gz | grep -E 'root/\.ssh/(config|authorized_keys)'
   # want -rw-r--r-- on both
   #+end_src

** DONE 2.3 build emacs-30.1-treesitter-ubuntu-24.04
   DONE 2026-09-14, built LOCALLY (host arch amd64 == target arch amd64,
   so plain =docker build= — no buildx/qemu, no proxy needed; direct
   internet confirmed reachable from this box).  NOT run on c02 — see
   the Group-1 deviation note.
   Produced =amd64.emacs30.1_24.04.tar.gz=, MEASURED 198 MiB (207167222
   bytes).  SMOKE-TESTED in a clean =ubuntu:24.04= container (separate
   shell from the build): unpack + =ldconfig= +
   =emacs --version= -> "GNU Emacs 30.1", =(princ emacs-version)= ->
   "30.1", vterm =require= -> "VTERM OK".  No Dockerfile changes needed
   for this build.

** DONE 2.5 build emacs-30.1-treesitter-arcadia-azurelinux-3.0-photon-5.0
   DONE 2026-09-14, built LOCALLY (see Group-1 deviation note).  TWO
   BUGS found and fixed here, both new findings not anticipated by this
   plan — details in
   =.github/REPL/fix.archive/emacs-bundle-arcadia-build-fixes.md=:
     1. Dockerfile's own header comment claimed gcc/make/tar/curl/
        zlib-devel/pkgconf were "already in base" — MEASURED FALSE for
        gcc, make, which (rpm -qa and a filesystem search both came up
        empty).  devbox-arcadia never invokes gcc/make so it never
        tripped over the same stale claim.  Added
        =gcc make which= to the =tdnf install -y= list.
     2. =amd64.tar.list= hardcoded exact shared-library filenames for
        libgnutls/libhogweed/libnettle (=.30.37.1=, =.6.8=, =.8.8=) that
        no longer match what the base image ships (=.30.42.0=, =.6.9=,
        =.8.9=) — base-image package updates drift these version
        suffixes.  Updated the three entries in =amd64.tar.list= to the
        MEASURED current versions.
   Produced =amd64.arcadia.emacs30.1_azl3.0.tar.gz=, MEASURED 265 MiB
   (277081286 bytes).  SMOKE-TESTED in a clean
   =codeexecutionjupyterext1:latest= container (separate shell): unpack
   + =ldconfig= + =emacs --version= -> "GNU Emacs 30.1", vterm =require=
   -> "VTERM OK".

** DONE 2.6 build devbox-arcadia-azurelinux-3.0-photon-5.0
   DONE 2026-09-14, built LOCALLY (see Group-1 deviation note).  ONE BUG
   found and fixed — details in
   =.github/REPL/fix.archive/emacs-bundle-arcadia-build-fixes.md=:
   =tar.sh='s npm-wrapper loop ran =readlink -f= on
   =$NPM_GPREFIX/bin/$cmd= UNCONDITIONALLY; GNU =readlink -f=
   canonicalizes even a non-existent path, so it emitted a phantom
   =usr/bin/tsserver= entry and =tar= aborted mid-archive.  ROOT CAUSE:
   the pinned =typescript@7.0.2= dropped the standalone =tsserver=
   binary (folded into the =tsc= CLI); =typescript-language-server=
   does not need it and still answers fine.  Fixed by guarding the loop
   with =[ -e "$NPM_GPREFIX/bin/$cmd" ] || continue= before resolving.
   Produced =amd64.arcadia.dev.base.azl3.0.tar.gz=, MEASURED 47 MiB
   (49034304 bytes) — comfortably the smallest of the three, as
   expected (no compiled Emacs inside).  SMOKE-TESTED in a clean
   =codeexecutionjupyterext1:latest= container (separate shell):
   =typescript-language-server --version= -> "6.0.0",
   =jedi-language-server --version= -> "0.47.0".  Also VERIFIED the
   2.2 fix landed in the artifact: =tar tvzf ... | grep root/\.ssh=
   shows =-rw-r--r--= on both =config= and =authorized_keys=.

** TODO 3.4 push the dot-emacs fixes UPSTREAM too
   USER RULING (answers "btw, the plan should be in dot-emacs also,
   right?"): yes — this plan changes dot-emacs, so dot-emacs must
   receive those changes, and the plan that explains them.
   TWO REPOS, DIFFERENT CONTENT — do not mirror blindly:
     - THIS repo (cluster) keeps the plan as the EXECUTION record: the
       fleet measurements, the archive/ bundles, the bin/ drop-ins.
       Those are cluster facts and mean nothing upstream.
     - dot-emacs receives the SOURCE FIXES (2.5 endpoint, 2.6 modes)
       plus a short build note in its own =build/= folder — it already
       carries =build/project.org.txt=, so that is where a build-level
       document belongs, next to the recipes it describes.
   :trap: do NOT push cluster's fleet/box details upstream.  This is a
   public repo; box names, internal endpoints and credential routes
   are not its business.  Send the fix, not the environment.
   :trap: this is the step 1.0's key gate exists for — if 1.0 was
   skipped, everything up to here still "worked" and only this fails.

* TODO Group 4 — drop in, both tiers, then verify
** TODO 4.1 write bin/wsl-emacs.sh (WSL tier drop-in)
   Idempotent, like container-tmux.sh: a tier that already has a working
   emacs is a no-op.

** TODO 4.2 write bin/container-emacs.sh (container tier drop-in)
   Same shape; =docker cp= + unpack at /, then assert the artifact runs.
   :PORT_CONVENTION, so the executor does not rediscover this the hard
   way (I did, this session):
     | 22   | Windows sshd   | =cNNwin= |
     | 2200 | WSL distro     | =cNNwsl= |
     | 2222 | container sshd | =cNN=    (BARE name, like helix/devcontainer) |
   There is NO =ctr= tier and NO port 2224.  2224 was correct only while
   the distro held 2222; the distro moved to 2200 and vacated it.
   :trap: A =~/.ssh/config= ON DISK MAY PREDATE THE FIX.  =bin/fleet.py=
   is the generator and is authoritative — REGENERATE, never read:
       python3 bin/fleet.py sshconfig > ~/.ssh/config
   MEASURED after regenerating: =ssh c01= lands on Microsoft Azure Linux
   3.0 (c01, c02).  c03/c04 run no container, so they are legitimately
   (unreachable) at that tier — not a failure of this plan.
   So the VERIFY half of this item is plain ssh (or =-t ""= through the
   wrapper); =docker cp= is only needed for the WRITE half.

** TODO 4.3 fan both out and read the table
   #+begin_src bash
   .github/skills/fleet_ssh/fleet-ssh.sh \
     EMACS='emacs --version | head -1' \
     TSLS='typescript-language-server --version 2>/dev/null || echo -' \
     JEDI='jedi-language-server --version 2>/dev/null || echo -'
   #+end_src
   :trap: UNIFORM COLUMNS ARE WHAT A BROKEN PROBE LOOKS LIKE.  This
   session was bitten twice — a quoting-death awk returned NONE on 4/4
   while the fleet was fine, and a wrong tmux socket returned "-" on
   4/4.  If every box answers identically, prove the probe works by
   running it manually on one box before believing the table.

** TODO 4.4 verify ssh still works after the drop-in
   The devbase tarball overwrites =/root/.ssh/config=,
   =authorized_keys= and =/etc/ssh= — i.e. it can lock you out of the
   box it just landed on.
   :hard-rule: back up the existing ssh material BEFORE unpacking, and
   verify on ONE box with a SECOND session already open, never by
   closing the only session you have.  Only then fan out.

** TODO 4.5 verify .bashrc sources cleanly AND its endpoint answers
   Two separate checks — see the trap in :BASHRC_PATCH_SHIPS_A_DEAD_IP:.
   =bash -lc true= proves syntax; it does NOT prove the provider URL is
   alive.  Probe the endpoint itself.

* Main Loop
  With :test_tool: =bin/emacs-bundle-status.sh= ready:
    - (R) read the per-box table; find the tier/box that is not green
    - (E) fix in the build recipe or the drop-in script, rebuild that
          ONE tarball
    - (P) re-run the test_tool in a SEPARATE shell from the build
    - (L) until every box answers in both tiers

  Stop conditions that are NOT success:
    - a uniform column (see 4.3 trap)
    - "the file is there" without the binary running
    - ssh verified only from the session that was already open
